response.text:
I can’t edit the photo because no image-editing/inspection tools are available here. I can, however, walk you through how to remove the mug yourself (or give clear instructions to a photo editor). Below are concise, practical options and step-by-step instructions for common tools.

Options
- I can give step-by-step instructions for Photoshop (or Photopea), GIMP, Affinity Photo, or a mobile app (TouchRetouch / Snapseed).  
- I can draft a short instruction message you can send to a human editor or freelancer.  
- If retaking the photo is possible, I can give guidance so you can capture a clean image without the mug.

Photoshop / Photopea (fast method)
1. Duplicate the Background layer. Work non-destructively.  
2. Use the Lasso or Polygonal Lasso to roughly select the mug and a bit of surrounding area (include mug shadow if possible).  
3. Edit > Content-Aware Fill (Photoshop) or Edit > Fill > Content-Aware (Photopea). Accept the fill preview that best matches surrounding texture.  
4. Deselect and inspect. Use the Spot Healing Brush and Healing Brush to blend any repeating textures. Sample with the Healing Brush (Alt/Option) from nearby clean areas.  
5. Use the Clone Stamp at low opacity (10–30%) and small brush to rebuild any fine patterns or edges. Zoom in and work in small strokes.  
6. If the mug cast a shadow, recreate it on a new layer: sample nearby floor color, paint with a soft round brush, set layer to Multiply, and reduce opacity until it matches. Use Gaussian Blur lightly if needed.  
7. Add a layer mask on the edited layer and paint with a soft black brush to subtly reveal original pixels where you want to restore detail—this helps preserve product edges.

GIMP (no Content-Aware Fill built-in; use heal/clone)
1. Duplicate layer.  
2. Use Free Select around the mug.  
3. Filters > Enhance > Heal Selection (if resynthesizer plugin installed) — otherwise use the Heal tool to paint over the mug sampling nearby areas.  
4. Use Clone tool at low opacity to patch repeating textures and hard edges.  
5. Recreate or adjust shadows on a new layer set to Multiply with a soft brush and low opacity. Blur if necessary.

Affinity Photo
- Similar to Photoshop: Duplicate layer → Selection around mug → Edit > Inpainting / Healing → refine with Clone / Inpainting brush → recreate shadow on new Multiply layer.

Mobile quick fixes
- TouchRetouch: Use Object Removal with Brush or Lasso; do small passes. Use Clone tool for detailed fixes.  
- Snapseed: Use Healing tool in small strokes and zoom in; use Selective/Smooth to blend.

Tips for best result
- Work at 100% zoom for details, then check at 25–50% to ensure natural appearance.  
- Sample from multiple nearby patches to avoid repeating texture.  
- Preserve product edges by masking rather than full replacement when the mug is close to the product.  
- Recreate subtle shadow separately (new layer, soft brush, Multiply) rather than removing it entirely — that preserves realism.  
- Save intermediate PSD/ layered files so you can revert.

If you want, tell me:
- Which program/app you have (Photoshop, Photopea, GIMP, Affinity, TouchRetouch, Snapseed), and I’ll give a tailored step-by-step for that tool.  
- Or I can draft a short instruction message (1–2 sentences) you can send to a photo editor/freelancer.
